name: Repono Ltd
tagline: Cheap, high-ROCE BSE-SME petroleum-storage/O&M play with a Reliance contract as a credential — SME liquidity and short history are the constraints
business_overview: Repono (BSE SME, 544463; incorporated 2017, listed Aug 2025) provides integrated operations & maintenance (O&M), logistics support and 360-degree warehousing / liquid-terminal services focused on the oil value chain (crude, ethanol, petrochemicals, lube blending, specialty chemicals, ATF) plus FFS polymer bagging. Small ValuePickr thread (6 posts) read to June 2026.
fundamentals_narrative: Genuinely attractive combination: ROCE ~27%, ROE ~22%, ~27% multi-year revenue CAGR, effectively debt-free, at a P/E of ~11.7 — cheap for the return profile. The main practical constraint is BSE-SME liquidity and a very short public history (listed Aug 2025). A supply/O&M agreement with Reliance Industries is a major credential, but per community discussion the revenue impact is ~3 years out (around 2029).
technical_read: Not independently pulled. 52-week range Rs 43-107; stock roughly 2.5x off its low with a mid-2026 rally that one community poster attributed partly to trader activity after a broker mention.
sentiment_summary: Small ValuePickr thread (6 posts, highest post #7), first-time read of all inline posts, spanning Dec 2025 to June 2026. Santosh_Kadam wrote the business primer; Chandan_Sharma linked the H1 FY26 concall transcript; deepakreads (June 2026) cautioned the current rally may be trader-driven and that the Reliance agreement will take ~3 years to show in numbers, while noting the promoters are pursuing a second large contract.
community_signal: No trusted-roster users in the thread. deepakreads' post is the most balanced: positive on the Reliance credential and pipeline, cautious on near-term rally sustainability and the long revenue-recognition lag.
bse_notes: Reliance Industries supply/O&M agreement disclosed; promoters reportedly pursuing a second large contract. Not independently verified this pass. BSE-SME listing — structurally thin liquidity.
bull_case: ROCE ~27% / ROE ~22% with a ~27% revenue CAGR, effectively debt-free, at only ~11.7x earnings
Reliance Industries agreement is a strong credential that materially upgrades the customer profile and pipeline credibility
Microcap (~Rs 79 Cr) — genuine 10x headroom if it graduates off SME and executes the contract pipeline
bear_case: BSE-SME liquidity is a hard, structural constraint on building or exiting any real position
Very short public track record (listed Aug 2025) — limited multi-quarter data
Reliance-contract revenue is ~3 years out; near-term rally may be substantially trader-driven
verdict_headline: Cheap, high-return SME with a real Reliance credential — fits the 10x frame, held to Medium by SME liquidity and a short history
verdict_reasoning: The fundamental package (ROCE ~27%, ~27% growth, debt-free, P/E ~11.7) plus a Reliance contract credential and a ~Rs 79 Cr base keeps this inside the 10x-in-2-3-years frame
Conviction is Medium, not higher: BSE-SME liquidity, ~1 year of public history, and a ~3-year lag on the flagship contract's revenue
Old 108-stock project rated this Tier A; re-derived under the open-screen thesis it still fits, with SME liquidity the unchanged binding constraint

four_box.note: Reliance Industries agreement is a strong credential but revenue impact ~3yrs out and near-term rally may be trader-driven — tailwind weak; microcap (~Rs79cr) base gives real tam headroom; no distinct moat beyond the Reliance credential — weak; P/E ~11.7x explicitly cheap for ROCE~27%/ROE~22% — valuation yes. BSE-SME liquidity + short public history are separate constraints.
